title: Code nothing uses
headline: There is little dead code: about 2,700 lines of 772,000 (0.35%), thin over some 400 files and dropped by the build, and none of it is a feature waiting for opening: it is code with no caller. The one run-time price is the 19,614-line schema that every cold start evaluates for a query builder nobody calls (150 to 190 ms and about 18 MB, measured here): three lines to change, the same fix as DS-1 and DP-1. The planner's own check added one cost the report missed: a unit test replays all 789 archived migrations on every run (6.2 s and about 630 MB, measured). The plan is a guard first (the review's scan as an exact-list ratchet, about 9 s a run), then deletion in tiers: 721 lines nothing uses, about 230 in three dead files, and about 1,700 that only a test keeps alive.

findings.title: Every cold start evaluates the 19,614-line schema that no query reads
findings.evidence: src/db/client.ts imports the whole schema as a value (line 11), uses it as a type (line 31) and hands it to drizzle (line 78). Nothing else imports it at run time: rg over src, scripts and e2e finds client.ts, one scan test (src/server/store-export.scan.test.ts:4) and drizzle.config.ts. No code uses the query builder: rg for db().select, .insert, .query and for $inferSelect or InferSelectModel finds nothing outside src/db; every query is raw SQL through execute. The skeptic timed the module three times on an esbuild bundle: 117 to 149 ms to evaluate and 16 MB of heap; drizzle's init with the schema 32 to 36 ms and 2.3 MB, against 0.03 to 0.04 ms without. In the finished build 6 server chunk files hold the schema (the planner re-ran rg -l -F orders_store_placed_idx over .next/server: 6).
findings.cost: 150 to 190 ms and about 18 MB on each cold start of a function that touches the database (measured on this machine on the schema alone; DS-1 and DP-1 measured 60 to 135 ms on whole routes; an estimate for Vercel either way), and about 0.8 MB of JavaScript in each of 6 server chunks (measured).
findings.who_pays: The server on every cold start, so the first shopper or owner to reach a fresh instance. Today that is mostly scheduled jobs and the team. It grows with stores, traffic spikes and deploys: more instances, more cold starts.

findings.title: Nothing counts unused code, so it grows unseen
findings.evidence: ESLint runs Next's two presets with --max-warnings 0: they fail on an unused local or import, never on an unused export. None of the 46 scan tests mentions unused, orphan or importers, and package.json has no tool for it. An export keyword on a name its own file does not use switches off the compiler's and the linter's check: that is the 263 plus 655 suspects, found only because a scanner was written for this review (256 lines on the repo's own TypeScript, 8.8 s over 6,191 files; it is in the repo at docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/unused-code.mjs). The other 2,205 over-exported names are used in their own file and hide nothing. Test support has no single name either: 9 of the 34 test-support files end in something the existing ratchet does not know (NOT_COUNTED, scripts/lib/ratchet-count.mjs:16), so src/server/trust-fixtures.ts is held to production rules with 5 unchecked reads in ratchet.baseline.json.
findings.cost: No budget: each unit adds a few helpers and word constants nothing reads. In 47 days that came to about 2,700 lines, about 57 a day.
findings.who_pays: Maintainers and agents, later: each dead name is a false lead in a search and context spent.
fix_steps: 1. Make the scan a library: copy docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/unused-code.mjs to scripts/lib/unused-scan.mjs and export unusedScan(root), which returns three sorted lists: unusedExports and testOnlyExports as 'file#name', testOnlyFiles as paths. Keep its rules as they are: entry points are Next's convention files under src/app, src/proxy.ts, src/instrumentation.ts, scripts/** and the config files; tests are *.test.*, *.spec.*, e2e/**, e2e-live/** and src/test/**; exports of convention files and register in src/instrumentation.ts are skipped; a namespace, star or dynamic import marks a whole file as used.

Then run node scripts/ratchet.mjs: src/server/trust-fixtures.ts leaves ratchet.baseline.json.

3. scripts/unused.mjs (the twin of scripts/ratchet.mjs): writes src/server/unused.baseline.json with four parts: unusedExports (list), testOnlyExports (list), keptForTests (an object 'file#name' to the reason a test needs it: an oracle, a guard list, a reset helper) and testOnlyFiles (an object path to reason, for files only tests reach that are not test support: i18n-glossary.ts, legal-wording-nb.ts, store-export-scope.ts, signature-themes.ts, experiment-legacy.ts today). It refuses to add an entry to the two lists unless run with --first, and prints what was removed.

4. src/server/unused.scan.test.ts: (a) every export the scan calls unused is in unusedExports, else the message says 'delete it or use it'; (b) every tests-only export is in testOnlyExports or keptForTests, else 'a helper only tests need lives in a *-test-support.ts file; an oracle is listed in keptForTests with its reason'; (c) every tests-only file that is not test support is in testOnlyFiles; (d) the baseline holds nothing that is no longer a suspect (run node scripts/unused.mjs), as the ratchet's fourth case does.

5. Write the first baseline as things stand (917 suspect exports, and the 9 files only tests reach that are not test support by name: five guard files, the three dead ones of DD-8 and migration-files.ts), with keptForTests filled from the oracles and seams the review named (buildInvoiceSnapshot, buildEditInvoiceSnapshot, creditNoteSnapshot, editCreditNote, nextState, validateExport, STORE_MATCHER, replayAgentEval, closeDb, forgetUpsTokens, resetTicks, the two registerProblems, SECRET_TABLES, NOT_EXPORTED). DD-3, DD-8 and DD-2 then shrink the lists.

6. CLAUDE.md, Conventions, one sentence: an export nothing imports is deleted; a helper only tests need lives in a *-test-support.ts file; unused.scan.test.ts holds both, and node scripts/unused.mjs lowers its baseline.

Scan tests with their own idea of a fixture (src/server/store-writers.scan.test.ts:18, tax-reports.scan.test.ts:18, theme-installs.scan.test.ts:22, order-edit-writers.scan.test.ts:20, src/lib/notification-readers.scan.test.ts:67): untouched; they can take TEST_SUPPORT when next edited.

Together 331 exports, 721 lines, in 209 files: 105 types, 89 functions (most one-line helpers), 116 other constants, 21 re-exports; 23 are server functions (158 lines). findings.evidence: Stored page JSON is upgraded on read from three older shapes: pages before rows (upgradeLegacy, 10 lines), rows and blocks before D179 (responsive.ts:398-529, 132 lines; upgradeColumn at :440 is already a no-op) and text settings before D180 (typography.ts:641-827, 187 lines). They run in z.preprocess on every row and block. The skeptic measured about 10 microseconds for a page of 12 rows and 120 blocks, so there is no real per-request cost. Two things keep them from being plain dead code. First, the heading branch is live: headingLook() (typography.ts:830) runs foldTypography so the AI page studio can write headings by preset name (page-ai.ts:766). Second, and missed by the report: today's code still writes one old shape. upgradeBlock() treats a grid's columns given as {mobile, tablet, desktop} as pre-D179 (responsive.ts:459 and :498-504), and six places in production code write exactly that (src/lib/signature/kit.ts:85, meridian.ts:371, atelier.ts:284, kinetic.ts:311, src/lib/content-pack-pages.ts:77 and :162), as does the seed (supabase/seed.sql:273 and :279). Upgrade-on-read is also a written rule (docs/responsive-editing.md:56, docs/rules/admin/website.md:38) and e2e/pages.spec.ts:8 writes the pre-rows shape on purpose. Production holds 1,389 pages and 642 versions; how many are in an old shape is not known.
findings.cost: About 240 removable lines and their tests, and two extra shapes to keep in mind when a block changes. About 10 microseconds per page read: nothing a shopper or the server would notice.

findings.title: Live drills can only be asked for by hand-written SQL, and their job polls every five minutes
findings.evidence: The only insert into commerce.live_drills is inside requestDrills() (live-drills.ts:45), and only its integration test calls requestDrills (rg over src: the definition and live-drills.int.test.ts). No page, action or assistant tool asks for a drill, and every read of the table is inside live-drills.ts, so no screen shows a result. This is close to what D406 intended: its reason is that the AI doing the development should be able to run live checks itself, which staff actions and the Admin API do not allow; that AI works through the database. The decision and the rule also name a platform admin, who has no door. The dispatcher runs the job on every pass (route.ts:220). An idle run is two small queries (settleDreamDrills and the claim at lines 390-401); production's cron_jobs gives 158 ms for its last run, inside a dispatcher run that happens anyway.
findings.cost: Two queries and about 160 ms inside each five-minute dispatcher run: about 45 seconds of function time a day, the same whatever the store count. No extra function run. A request made by SQL skips requestDrills' own checks, though the runner checks test mode again (line 404).
findings.who_pays: The server and database every five minutes, a little; the platform team, who must write SQL to ask and to read the result.
fix_steps: Owner's choice, A or B. Neither is urgent.

A (give it a door). On the platform's store page (src/app/admin/(gated)/platform/stores/[store]/) add a Run drills form, shown only when the store's checkout is in Stripe's test mode, whose action runs through platformAction() and calls requestDrills(storeId, kinds, account.id); below it the last five rows of commerce.live_drills (status, finished, each result's line) read through typedRows(). Add a tool to the platform's assistant that calls the same function, with the prompt-safety rule and a case in the agents' eval. Words in the platform catalogue in both languages.

B (keep it a console tool on purpose). Say so where it is described: docs/rules/admin/platform.md:233, D406 in docs/decisions.md and the comment at src/server/live-drills.ts:31 say 'asked for by an insert into commerce.live_drills, read from the row', and drop 'a platform admin'. No code changes.

The polling is not this finding's to fix: CR-2 in the scheduled-work plan gives each dispatcher job a cadence, and a job with a queue runs only when a row waits. Under that plan runLiveDrills() runs when commerce.live_drills has a row with status 'requested' or a waiting dream-factory result.
